At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
All security disciplines work under the umbrella of the combined PSI (Platform, Security & Infrastructure) team: we build the paved path and tooling that hundreds of engineers around the world rely on every day to ship. Corporate Security owns the estate everyone at Flexport actually touches — the laptops, the identity provider, the SaaS sprawl, the browser. Get it right and nobody notices. Get it wrong and it's the fastest way into everything else we're trying to protect.
This is a security engineering role, not an IT support role. You'll spend your time writing code and shipping automation, not administering a helpdesk queue or babysitting a ticket tray.
What you'll do
Identity & access
Advance our identity posture: SSO coverage, phishing-resistant MFA rollout, SCIM lifecycle automation, and least-privilege access across the SaaS and cloud estate.
Build the detections and guardrails that catch account takeover, MFA fatigue attacks, and session token theft before they turn into incidents.
Endpoint & device lifecycle
Write and ship device policy as code — configuration profiles, remediation scripts, and enforcement rules across macOS and Windows — with staged rollout and rollback built in from day one.
Maintain and improve our EDR stack's detection and response coverage across the fleet.
SaaS posture
Reduce SaaS risk at scale through SSPM tooling and automation , including detection of risky OAuth grants, shadow IT, and configuration drift across our critical SaaS applications.
Own security configuration for the SaaS tools hundreds of Flexporters use daily (Google Workspace, Slack, and similar), and keep pace as we add AI agents and MCP integrations to that surface.
Automation & enablement
Automate the parts of corporate security that don't need a human — device provisioning, access reviews, vendor security questionnaires — so the team scales with headcount instead of straining against it.
Write runbooks and documentation that make the rest of the team more capable , and partner with IT and People teams to ship controls that don't create the friction that drives people to workarounds.
You should have
Typically 2–5 years of experience in corporate, enterprise, or IT security engineering — we care more about what you've shipped than the exact number. If you meet most of this, apply; we'd rather see your work than filter you out on a résumé line.
Hands-on experience with modern endpoint management and EDR tooling (Jamf, Kandji, Intune, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, or similar).
Working knowledge of identity protocols (SAML, OIDC, SCIM) and a major identity provider (Okta, Entra, Google Workspace, or similar).
Comfort writing real code or scripts (Python, Go, or similar) to replace manual, ticket-driven work with automation.
Clear, practical communicator who can explain a control tradeoff to an engineer, a salesperson, and a VP without changing the facts.
Nice to have
Experience with SSPM tooling and OAuth-grant governance.
Exposure to DLP or insider-risk tooling.
Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) for managing security configuration.

description:
Headquarters: United States - Remote
Tebra only initiates contact with candidates via email from an official Tebra email address (@ tebra.com , @ patientpop.com , or @ kareo.com ) or through our applicant tracking system, Greenhouse. We will only ask you to provide sensitive personal information through our official application portal — not via social media or text message. We do not conduct interviews via instant messaging.
About the Role
Tebra helps private practices bring modernized care to patients everywhere. To run our own business well, every team needs numbers it can trust.
We're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to help build Tebra's new internal analytics platform. You'll turn data from Salesforce, NetSuite, Stripe, our product, and other systems into one shared, tested set of business data and metrics that Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments all use. You'll lead projects end to end, set the standards others build on, and partner with business leaders to define the metrics that matter most.
Your Area of Focus
Data Modeling & Shared Datasets: Design, build, and maintain enterprise-wide business data that teams across Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments build on. Apply dimensional modeling and layered design (staging, intermediate, and marts) so business logic lives in one place and isn't rebuilt by each team.
Metric Definition & Semantic Layer: Partner with metric owners in Finance and the business to define each key metric once, with a named owner and documented logic. Publish governed metrics in a semantic layer that Tableau, AI assistants, and other tools query, and reconcile them to current reporting and the general ledger before teams switch over.
Self-Service Enablement: Build easy-to-use datasets that let non-technical teammates and analysts answer their own questions without writing complex joins.
Platform Migration: Lead projects end to end on the new internal analytics platform, from source data to dashboards. Move each team's reporting over one domain at a time, with clear cutover and rollback plans, and onboard the analysts who contribute to new conventions, review processes, and tools.
Data Quality & Testing: Build automated tests and pull-request checks so data issues are caught before they reach reports. Monitor scheduled jobs, fix failures, and recover runs as part of shared production support.
Performance & Efficiency: Tune SQL, models, and pipeline schedules so data refreshes on time and dashboards load in seconds. Monitor compute usage and cost, and choose how each model is built and refreshed to keep both in check.
Forecasting & Machine Learning: Partner with analysts and data scientists to prepare clean, documented datasets for forecasting and machine learning models, such as retention and revenue projections.
Code Review & Mentorship: Review code from analysts and engineers across teams, and coach them on modeling, SQL, and testing standards.
Governance & Documentation: Follow data-sharing and privacy rules that keep protected health information (PHI) and personal data out of internal analytics. Maintain model documentation, lineage, and metric definitions via dbt, GitHub, Confluence, and Jira.
Your Professional Qualifications
Experience: 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar role, with 2+ years hands-on in dbt in production.
SQL Fluency: Expert SQL, including window functions, CTEs, and performance tuning for queries and pipelines on large datasets.
Data Modeling: Deep proficiency in dimensional modeling (Kimball), including shared datasets that serve many teams.
Tech Stack: Proven experience with Snowflake or a similar cloud data warehouse, and with dbt.
Business Partnership: Experience defining business metrics with Finance or business stakeholders, and reconciling data to financial systems.

In this role, you will own our clients' dbt architecture, standardizing how data is modeled, tested, documented, and deployed across their entire cloud data warehouse.
This role requires an engineer who treats analytics code like software: using version control, writing automated tests, optimizing warehouse compute costs, and implementing continuous integration (CI) pipelines. You will transform complex pipelines into dry, modular data environments that enable fast, accurate business decision-making.
What we are looking for:
3+ years of deep, hands-on production experience architecting complex dbt Core or dbt Cloud projects.
Master-level proficiency in writing highly complex, optimized, and readable SQL. Deep understanding of dimensional modeling (Kimball methodology), Data Vault 2.0, or wide-table strategies for analytics.
Proven track record in configuring and managing large datasets within modern platforms like Snowflake, Google BigQuery, or Databricks.

About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.
About the Query Team
Every pipeline, job, and test that runs on CircleCI generates data, and that history is one of our biggest advantages in an agentic software delivery lifecycle. Flaky test detection, test insights, pipeline search, and agents that reason about why a build failed all depend on fast, reliable access to it.
The Query team owns the system that makes this possible. We pull product data out of the transactional services that create it and store it in datastores built for historical and analytical workloads. We serve it through domain-level APIs to CircleCI's product teams and to customers through our public API. Our goal is to make storing data "fire and forget" for every other team, and querying it fast and dependable at a scale that keeps growing.
What You'll Do
Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
Shape how we store data at scale. Own and harden our ClickHouse-based storage layer. Design schemas for known and emerging access patterns, and tune ingestion and query performance to support production-scale data.
Build the pipelines that move our data. Design and own ingestion from event streams and durable workflows built on Temporal. Data should arrive reliably, stay queryable while it's in transit, and never slow down the critical path of the services that produce it.
Serve data to the product and to customers. Evolve our platform into the default path for historical queries. Make getting historical data easy, not a bottleneck. Teams should be able to get what they need quickly and with minimal hand-holding, while Query keeps enough visibility into how the data is used to optimize ingestion and reads across every consumer. Build in the indexing, caching, and tiered storage required to keep it performant.
Set technical direction. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you lead the design discussion, write up the architecture decision, and make the call. You help decide which data domain we migrate next and how.
Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand ingestion lag, query latency, and data correctness. For a data platform, operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
Keep things moving. You take ambiguous data problems from design to production quickly, and you help the people around you move faster too.
You don't just patch problems, you ask why they happened. You'll fix the immediate issue, then solve the underlying team practice, process, or system that let it through.
What You'll Bring
AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
Hands-on data experience. You've built or owned data-intensive systems such as ingestion pipelines, event-driven architectures, or analytical and time-series datastores. You understand the tradeoffs between transactional and analytical storage, and you've designed schemas and tuned queries for high-volume workloads. Experience with ClickHouse or another columnar database is a strong plus.

Own software engineering projects end-to-end on a highly autonomous, horizontally integrated team with a lot of leverage. This is a code-forward role!
Define what identity means for autonomous agents and other non-human actors at Discord (how they're provisioned, scoped, authenticated, authorized, and audited). As the role of these actors grows, and create primitives to implement that vision.
Build and evolve Access , Discord's employee authorization platform, to make permissions discoverable, role-based, least privilege, and self-serve; check out our blog post to learn more!
Design and harden our Zero Trust architecture, spanning human and service-to-service auth*n for Discord’s internal tooling.
Automate continuous permission right-sizing in the spirit of least privilege.
Develop and apply secure baselines for cloud identity, and help secure our software supply chain from the dev environment through CI/CD and into production.
Consult on risk assessments, architectural designs, threat models, code reviews, and more, pragmatically balancing security with other business considerations.
Example projects
Integrate service-to-service and agent-to-service authentication and authorization as out-of-the-box features in Discord's internal developer platform.
Build out service identity provisioning using PKI and mTLS, so services can authenticate each other without shared secrets.
Evaluate or extend infrastructure access tooling such as Teleport for short-lived, auditable access to hosts, databases, and internal systems.
Improve how secrets are issued, rotated, and scoped across our infrastructure.
What we look for
5+ years of experience building and operating production systems or infrastructure
3+ years of experience writing software in a general-purpose programming language (we mainly use Python, TypeScript, and Rust)
3+ years of experience securing systems with millions of users
Experience building or operating identity and access management systems: authentication, authorization, or access control at scale
Understanding of modern authentication and authorization concepts (e.g. RBAC, OAuth, OIDC, SSO, Zero Trust network architectures, mTLS, cloud IAM)
Experience building in and securing multi-cloud environments (e.g. GCP, Cloudflare, AWS)

Standardize tooling and infrastructure to improve the day-to-day developer experience.
Partner with other teams to raise test coverage, reliability, and speed across services.
Dig into application code to root-cause failures and drive fixes to completion.
Mentor and guide product engineers, fostering a culture of quality and continuous improvement.
Who You Are (Must-Haves)
You have 5+ years of experience as a software engineer building and maintaining production systems.
You have written code in strongly typed languages and have at least 1 year of experience with Go.
You are fluent with AI-assisted engineering - you actively use LLM-based tools in your workflow and have a clear point of view on where they elevate quality (and where they don’t).

title: Staff Network Engineer (AI Infrastructure)
description:
As a Staff Network Engineer at vCluster Labs , you aren't just configuring switches; you are building the automation logic that configures them. AI Clouds run on InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics that most teams still wire up by hand, one customer at a time. You will build the automation that turns that fabric into repeatable provisioning logic. You start in a small R&D group alongside our CTO and grow into owning this area as it becomes a core part of our platform.
As a Staff Network Engineer, your role will include:
Fabric automation: You will design and build the systems that automatically provision and configure NVIDIA switches and InfiniBand fabrics, including integration with NVIDIA UFM. Manual, per-customer switch setup is the thing you are replacing.
Network config management and sync: You will build the control loop that keeps switch, VLAN, and VXLAN state consistent with what our platform intends, detects drift, and reconciles it safely in production.
NAT gateway and L4 load balancing: You will build the gateway and load balancing layer that tenant clusters depend on for connectivity, with failover designed in from day one rather than bolted on later.
Scale and failure engineering: You will define how our network layer behaves at large scale: BGP route table limits, convergence, failover, and what happens when a link, switch, or gateway dies under real AI workloads.
Customer Zero for AI networking: You will run your automation on real AI Cloud environments, bring back what breaks, and turn hard-won operational lessons into product behavior our customers never have to think about.
Technical direction: You will help decide what we build versus integrate with partner solutions, write the design and requirements docs, and set the standards for how networking works across vCluster products.
This role could be a fit for you if you bring:
You have built network automation, not just operated networks: You have shipped software that configures switches, routers, or load balancers programmatically, ideally as part of a product or internal platform other teams relied on.
NVIDIA networking experience: Hands-on work with NVIDIA UFM, NVIDIA Spectrum or Quantum switches, Cumulus Linux, or NVUE, including programming against their APIs.
Deep fabric fundamentals: Strong command of InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, including how they behave and fail at production scale.
Production scale scars: You have run networks at real production scale, seen them break, and helped fix the root cause with automation rather than runbooks.
Software engineering ability: You write production code in Go or Python, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and think of network config as code.
Bonus points for:
AI networking depth: Experience tuning fabrics for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, congestion control, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X.
AI Cloud or hyperscaler background: You helped build network automation at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, or large CDN.
Load balancer and gateway internals: Experience building L4 load balancers or NAT gateways, including with eBPF/XDP or DPDK.
Open source: Contributions to networking or Kubernetes projects such as SONiC, FRRouting, Cilium, or MetalLB.
About vCluster Labs
We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

title: Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

Fill in client security questionnaires and build a reusable answer set.
Join selected client meetings or calls as a senior security voice when needed.

Run short internal workshops on key topics (for example OWASP Top 10, threat modeling, secure CI/CD).
Recommend training and certification paths for developers, Security Champions and DevOps engineers.

description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW
Our client is building the software that hearing clinics run on patient records, bookings, hearing tests and sales. Clinic chains and hospitals use it every day. You join the team that owns the Sales domain: quote, invoice, insurance claim and payment. We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer who ships business outcomes, not just tickets. You own features end to end - from why a clinic needs them, through design and build, to checking in production that they worked. AI coding agents are a normal part of every step of your work.
Tech environment: C# / .NET 8.0, Azure Services (Azure SQL, AI Search, Service Bus, App Insights, Data Factory), Entity Framework Core, Docker, Kubernetes, MassTransit, React with TypeScript, plus growing use of Python for AI tooling and experimentation.
IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL
Design, build and run full-stack features in the Sales domain: .NET services, event-driven integrations and React front end.
Work with the Product Owner and QA from discovery onwards. Shape the spec and agree acceptance criteria before code is written.
Find the gaps in a spec before you build. Close the small ones yourself and bring only business questions to the Product Owner.
Use AI tools across the whole lifecycle: planning, design, build, testing, review and maintenance. Keep the human judgement on correctness, security and data protection.
Own quality: unit and integration tests, code review, and non-functional requirements (performance, security, observability) as part of the design.
Follow features into production: watch telemetry and usage, support releases, investigate incidents and close the loop with the product team.
Contribute to architecture discussions and decision records with the Tech Lead and architects and help pay down tech debt in the sales flows.
Make the team better at AI: mentor engineers and share the instructions, checks and small tools that work.
Product Mindset
As AI takes on more of the typing, the value of an engineer moves to judgement: knowing what to build, why, and what good looks like for the user. In this role you:
Start every feature with the business question: who in the clinic uses it, and what problem it solves for them.
Push back with alternatives when a request is expensive and a simpler solution gives most of the value.
Explain technical trade-offs in business terms to Product Owners, delivery and customer-facing colleagues.
Look at usage, support tickets and customer feedback after release, and feed what you learn into the next iteration.
IF YOU ARE
Typically 5+ years of software engineering experience , with a strong track record of building and running production systems. We value practical experience and demonstrated capabilities over years alone.
Strong hands-on experience with C# and modern .NET , including:
Core and Web APIs.
Entity Framework / Entity Framework Core.
Clean Architecture and maintainable application design.
Solid frontend development experience using React and TypeScript , particularly for complex business applications.
Practical experience designing and developing microservices architectures .
Understanding of asynchronous communication and event-driven systems, ideally using:
Azure Service Bus.
MassTransit.
Similar messaging and event-processing technologies.
Strong SQL database experience, including relational data modelling and transactional business data.
Experience with API design, automated testing, debugging, and security fundamentals.
Hands-on experience using AI coding agents as part of everyday development, such as:
Ability to demonstrate practical AI-assisted development workflows, including examples of reviewing AI-generated code, identifying mistakes, and understanding when AI should not be used.
Strong product mindset, with examples of contributing to feature definition, understanding business needs, and influencing technical and product decisions.
Good command of English (B2 or above), both written and spoken.

title: AI Researcher — Distillation
description:
About the Role
We’re looking for an AI Researcher focused on model distillation to help us push the frontier of efficient, high-performance models. You’ll work on turning large, expensive models into smaller, faster, and more deployable systems—while maintaining or improving quality.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys publishing research , working close to real systems, and seeing their ideas move from papers → code → production.
What You’ll Work On
Design and evaluate model distillation techniques (teacher–student training, self-distillation, layer-wise distillation, representation matching, etc.)
Research tradeoffs between model size, latency, memory, and accuracy
Develop novel distillation approaches for:
Large language models
Long-context or specialized architectures
Inference-constrained environments
Run large-scale experiments and ablations; analyze results rigorously
Collaborate with engineers to productionize research outcomes
Write and submit research papers to top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, COLM, etc.)
Contribute to internal research notes, technical blogs, and open-source projects when appropriate
What We’re Looking For
Required
Strong background in machine learning research
Hands-on experience with model distillation or closely related topics (compression, pruning, quantization, representation learning)
Publication experience (conference or journal papers, workshop papers, or arXiv preprints)
Solid understanding of deep learning fundamentals (optimization, training dynamics, generalization)
Fluency in PyTorch (or equivalent) and research-grade experimentation
Ability to clearly communicate research ideas, results, and limitations
Nice to Have
Experience distilling large language models
Work on efficiency-focused research (latency, memory, throughput)
Experience with long-context models or non-Transformer architectures
Open-source contributions in ML or research tooling
Prior startup or applied research experience
Why Join Us
Real ownership over research direction at a Series A stage
Strong support for publishing and open research
Tight feedback loop between research and real-world deployment
Access to meaningful compute and production-scale problems
Small, highly technical team with deep ML and systems expertise
Example Backgrounds
ML researchers from academia transitioning to industry
Research engineers with published work in model efficiency
PhD / Post-doc graduates or industry researchers who still want to publish

title: Counterintelligence Technology & Program SME — AI Evaluation (Contract)
description:
Role Title: Counterintelligence Technology & Program SME — AI Evaluation (Contract)
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote
micro1 is engaging Counterintelligence Technology & Program SME — AI Evaluation (Contract)s to contribute critical subject matter expertise to a customer's project focused on the development and evaluation of advanced AI systems for security applications. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.
Scope of Work
Author and classify case studies at the counterintelligence boundary, distinguishing legitimate threat detection and analysis from prohibited personal surveillance or attribute-based targeting.
Apply program and technology-level judgement to assess how counterintelligence capabilities are constructed, authorized, and where outputs may exceed acceptable boundaries.
Evaluate AI outputs on source handling, analytical reasoning, recognition of limitations, and utility for surveillance or targeting tasks.
Ensure cases accurately reflect real-world counterintelligence practice, legal authorities, and oversight frameworks, not dramatized scenarios.
Identify and document instances where AI models improperly reject valid security or threat-analysis queries.
Thoroughly record edge cases and provide the underpinning authorities for each determination to ensure defensibility.
Preferred Qualifications
Senior-level counterintelligence background in US or allied agencies, services, or commands, with involvement in CI operations, technical CI, insider-threat analysis, or program leadership.
Demonstrated experience leading counterintelligence technology programs or technical threat-assessment initiatives (e.g., technical collection-threat, insider-threat tooling, supply-chain/acquisition security).
Strong understanding of foreign-intelligence threats, CI authorities, oversight regimes, and the nuanced line separating legitimate activities from prohibited surveillance or targeting.
Experience with program management or technical leadership, demonstrating real ownership over operational decisions.
Background in teaching, briefing, or conducting high-level analytic reviews in the CI domain.
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with emphasis on well-documented analysis.
Additional expertise in technical CI (TSCM, cyber CI, technical surveillance), cross-domain CI/intelligence, or prior participation in AI evaluation, wargaming, or red teaming is a plus.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
About the Role
Join a data and infrastructure team building a platform that turns information from multiple sources into reliable, current company intelligence. You will own the platform across architecture, ingestion, and production operations, helping deliver trusted data for downstream products.
What You'll Do
Design and build a multi-source data platform for concurrent ingestion, event-driven processing, and orchestrated batch workflows.
Develop resilient intake from provider APIs, webhooks, files, and web scraping, including rate limits and failure handling.
Orchestrate scheduled workflows and historical backfills using tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect.
Build event-driven systems with messaging and task queues, including retries, dead-letter handling, and controlled replay.
Store original payloads in cloud object storage and transform data with dbt into raw, standardized, and curated layers.
Implement idempotent upserts, data contracts, automated validation, pipeline tests, and monitoring for freshness and failures.
Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and loading patterns, and integrate enrichment and LLM-based structured extraction.
What We're Looking For
At least 5 years building and operating production data platforms, with ownership from architecture through deployment and ongoing operations.
Hands-on production experience with dbt and Google Cloud Platform, plus workflow orchestration such as Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, or Temporal.
Experience with event-driven systems, messaging or task queues, asynchronous processing, retries, and failure recovery.
Strong Python skills, including asynchronous HTTP and concurrent processing with tools such as asyncio, aiohttp, or HTTPX.
Strong SQL and PostgreSQL skills, including data modeling, query optimization, and incremental loading.
Experience with data contracts, raw and curated storage, retention policies, automated testing, and pipeline monitoring.
Startup or small-team experience, with broad ownership and changing priorities; web scraping, entity resolution, and data enrichment experience are helpful.
Compensation & Benefits
Base salary: $80,000 to $120,000 annually. Visa sponsorship is not available.
Location
Remote within Latin America.
Compensation Range: $80K - $120K

The developer will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving cross-platform mobile applications, managing day-to-day development of the apps and its backend, and ensuring a reliable user experience across Android and iOS.
You will serve as the primary developer, taking ownership of development and the codebase, implementing new features, fixing issues, and maintaining overall application performance. You will work closely with a QA tester and the company founder to plan, develop, test, and deliver updates.

Design and develop new mobile applications from the ground up for Android and iOS.
Build, maintain, and improve cross-platform applications using modern mobile development technologies.
Develop new features, improve existing functionality, troubleshoot technical issues, and resolve bugs.

Develop web-based applications and administrative platforms.

Identify technical improvements, investigate complex problems, and implement effective solutions.

Minimum 3 years of professional mobile application development experience.
Proven experience developing and publishing at least one React Native / Expo application on both Google Play and the Apple App Store. Applicants must provide links to previously published applications.

Practical experience building and maintaining backend systems, relational databases, APIs, and server-side functionality.

Experience developing responsive user interfaces and maintaining consistent application behavior across different devices.

description:
About ElevenLabs
ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.
We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.
Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.
How we work
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.
What we offer
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.
Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.
About the role
We are looking for a backend-leaning full-stack engineer to help build the next generation of Creative Agents at ElevenLabs.
Our ambition is to make agents a primary way people create across ElevenCreative. We are building systems that turn ideas into high-quality audio, image and video, bringing models and creative tools together without requiring users to become prompting experts.
The creative agent is already live. You will join a small team shaping its capabilities and architecture, with ownership from backend systems and agent infrastructure through to the customer-facing experience. You will help discover what works, turn experiments into reliable features, and use real customer feedback to guide what we build next.
Your responsibilities will include:
Building production agents and expanding their capabilities through prompts, tool use, orchestration, new models and MCP integrations.
Designing and operating reliable backend systems for asynchronous creative generation and long-running tasks, with strong performance, observability, scalability and security.
Developing shared evaluations and live quality monitoring, including model-based assessment of image and video outputs.
Owning features end to end, from identifying user needs and prototyping to shipping across the stack and supporting them in production, alongside product, design and engineering.

title: AI Platform Engineer
description:
About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
About the Role
We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.
Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.
The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.
This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.
You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.
What You'll Be Responsible For
In this role, you'll:
Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.
Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.
Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.
Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.
Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.
Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

title: FinOps Data Engineer
description:
About the Role
We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.
What You'll Be Responsible For
In this role, you'll:
Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.
Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on.
Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online.
Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match.
Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.
Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.
Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.
Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.
Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing).
Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb.
Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash.
Are comfortable with cost/billing tooling: AWS Cost Explorer, Cost & Usage Reports, GCP Billing Reports, and BI/dashboarding (we use Hex).
Have experience with, or are comfortable picking up, Linear and Notion as the system of record for tracking and documenting FinOps work.
Experience with a dedicated cloud cost management platform (e.g. CloudZero, Vantage, or similar) is a plus, not required.
Can analyze cost data and present it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

title: Solution Engineer
description:
Who We Are
At RelationalAI , we’re solving one of the most important challenges in artificial intelligence: how to teach large language models the logic, semantics, and business context of the modern enterprise.
Frontier models are trained almost entirely on public data — they can speak about the world, but they don’t understand your business. We fix that.
RelationalAI has pioneered a breakthrough called Superalignment — technology that enables LLMs to learn natively from private, structured enterprise data inside the data cloud.
By combining this with relational knowledge graphs and our proprietary neuro/symbolic-relational reasoners , we deliver trustworthy decision intelligence : systems that use semantic models to truly understand how a business operates and can reason across its data to drive better outcomes.
We’re a globally distributed team of engineers, scientists, and builders redefining how AI learns from data. We believe that high-stakes decisions deserve frontier intelligence — intelligence that’s explainable, aligned, and grounded in reality.
If you’re driven by curiosity, thrive in complexity, and want to help build the system that brings true understanding to enterprise AI, you’ll feel right at home here.
The Role
You will be embedded inside our customers' hardest problems, and you will own the outcome until it works in production.
You'll sit with executives, domain experts, and data teams to find the decisions that actually move their business - inventory that's in the wrong place, risk concentrations nobody can see, fraud patterns that only emerge across three systems, capacity plans built on guesses. Then you'll model their world in our ontology, formulate the reasoning problem, write the PyRel, and ship something that runs against their real data in their own Snowflake account.
Every engagement here produces two deliverables.
The first is the one the customer sees: a working decision system that changes how they operate.
The second is the one that matters most to us: the pile of things you had to invent because our platform didn't have them yet. The modelling pattern you hand-rolled. The constraint formulation that should have been a primitive. The three-hour workaround where an API should have existed. You bring those back, you argue for them, and the strongest of them become product.
That second deliverable is why this role exists. If you only ever deliver the first one, we've hired a consultant. We're not hiring consultants.
You'll operate with unusual autonomy: you decide what's worth building, when a workaround is acceptable and when it's technical debt we'll regret, and when to tell a customer their real problem is not the one they asked about. You'll be technical enough that when something breaks in a customer environment, you find the root cause yourself rather than filing a ticket and waiting.
What You'll Do
Own outcomes end to end - discovery, modelling, implementation, performance tuning, production hardening, and the measurement that proves it worked. Not a handoff at each stage. Yours.
Build, not describe - design and ship decision solutions on our modelling, reasoning, and learning stack: ontologies over customer data, rules, graph analytics, optimisation formulations, predictive models
Fill the gaps yourself - when a customer workflow is blocked on something the platform doesn't do, scope it and build it. Then push the general version upstream: read our source, form a hypothesis before you escalate, open the PR.
Close the loop with Product - every deployment generates a signal. Bring back reproductions, patterns, and specific failure modes ("the only way I could express this was by abusing X in this way"), not vibes. You are one of the loudest inputs into our roadmap.
Run technical discovery that gets to the truth - workshops, demos, and proofs of concept designed to find out whether we can actually solve the problem, not to look impressive.

About the Role
We're looking for a FinOps Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the Terraform or Lambda that ships the fix, working on a product feature chasing a number until it reconciles, and influencing product decisions when cost to reliability tradeoffs hit. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.
What You'll Be Responsible For
In this role, you'll:
Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.
Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.
Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.
Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.
Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards engineering and finance can both read.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.
Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash
Are comfortable with cost/billing tooling: AWS Cost Explorer, Cost & Usage Reports, GCP Billing Reports, and BI/dashboarding (we use Hex).

Can analyze cost data and present it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Have prior experience in a FinOps, cloud cost management, or cloud governance role.
Are energized by doing the unglamorous, high-leverage work (the schlep) that unblocks other teams, and by working cross-functionally without positional authority.

description:
About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
About the Role
We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using.
Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors.
This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.
What You'll Be Responsible For
Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python.
Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list.
Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope.
Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases.
Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it.
Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics.
Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog.
Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump.
Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents , which are now a major consumer of it.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any .
Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on.
Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked.
Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers.
Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml , wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly.
Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test.
Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default.
Have real autonomy: you find the important work, scope it, ship it, and say what you didn't do.

This job post is for future opportunities. If there isn’t an active opening that fits your skill set or location, you can still express interest in future roles with Testlio. Our Talent Acquisition team will keep your information on file and reach out if a suitable opportunity becomes available.
Typical Project Details:
Project Focus : Most QA Tester roles involve manual testing of mobile apps and APIs, typically within Agile development teams.
Project Duration : Contracts can be temporary, ranging from 6 months to 1 year, or ongoing. Many temporary projects extend beyond their initial term, and some evolve into ongoing contractor opportunities.
Location : This job ad is open to candidates in select countries who are comfortable working in a fully remote setup. Countries we are considering consist of Argentina, Brazil, Canada, the Czech Republic, Estonia, India, Ireland, Mexico, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, or the United States.
Schedule : Opportunities are available for both part-time and full-time contracts. Working hours generally follow day or afternoon schedules based on your regional time zone.
Timezone : While we support flexible work, most roles align with standard daytime hours in their region (e.g., 9 AM–6 PM). For instance, this may mean Central Standard Time (CST) in the Americas or Central European Time (CET) in EMEA. Please ensure your availability aligns with your region’s core hours.
Required Devices : You must have access to an Android or iOS mobile device for testing.
Internet Connection : A reliable, high-speed internet connection is required for testing and team communications. Mobile hotspots and other unstable or limited connections are not suitable.
What Your Day Looks Like
Execute smoke, scripted, and exploratory test cases on mobile, web, and desktop platforms.
Conduct functional, localization, regression, or payment testing to ensure software applications meet quality standards.
Reproduce issues found during testing.
Document and report test results, including bugs and potential risks. Clearly communicate findings to the development team and stakeholders.
Configure and prepare test environments per the provided instructions.
Work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure software products are delivered on time and meet customer expectations.
Design and optimize appropriate test data.
Provide clear feedback about outdated, incomplete, or inefficient test cases.
Stay updated with industry trends and advancements in software testing methodologies and tools.
What You’ll Need to Succeed
Technical Skills:
Proven experience (2+ years) as a Software Tester or similar role, with a strong understanding of software testing principles, methodologies, and tools (such as Jira, TestRail, Xray, or similar).
Experience with mobile and web applications frontend testing; backend testing is a bonus.
Proficiency in identifying and documenting software bugs and issues.
Ability to solve basic technical tasks required during testing, such as test data generation, log capturing, and basic analysis, working with browser developer tools, network logs analyzers, etc.
Experience working in agile teams in a remote environment - proven track record of communication and collaboration with stakeholders such as Scrum Masters, Product Owners, and others.
Good understanding of SDLC.

title: 1775 RPG/AS400 & JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Developer
description:
This is a remote position.
We are looking for a professional with hands-on experience developing in RPG/RPGLE on IBM AS400/iSeries, as well as proven experience with JD Edwards EnterpriseOne development tools.
We are not looking for an infrastructure administrator, a JD Edwards functional consultant, or an AS400 developer without JD Edwards experience. The ideal candidate must be able to work technically across both platforms, troubleshoot production issues, modify existing customizations, and participate in system integrations.
Responsibilities
Develop, modify, debug, and maintain RPG, RPGLE, and CL programs on IBM AS400/iSeries.

Named Event Rules (NERs)

Business Views

Provide technical and functional support to internal users.
Participate in JD Edwards upgrades, ESU installations, patch deployments, and system enhancements.
Prepare technical documentation, development specifications, and support procedures.
Maintain source code and technical objects following development best practices and coding standards.
Collaborate with functional teams, infrastructure teams, and business users to identify, analyze, and resolve operational needs.

Minimum of 3 years of professional experience developing on IBM AS400/iSeries.
Proven hands-on experience with:
RPG
RPGLE
CL

Strong knowledge of JD Edwards development tools, including:

Business View Design
UBE Design
Business Functions

Table Conversions

title: Solutions Architect for Automotive
description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1000+ colleagues in 70+ countries and very few roles based in offices. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder led, profitable and growing. We are hiring a Solutions Architect for Automotive to help our partners (companies like Mercedes, Ford, GM, Elektrobit, Intel, Nvidia, Google, Dell, HP, Accenture, Tata and the like) and prospects understand and embrace our open source platform for themselves and their customers.
Our worldwide field engineering team apply expert insights to real-world customer problems, enabling the enterprise adoption of Ubuntu, OpenStack, Kubernetes, AI/MLOps and a wide range of associated technologies. We are experts in the whole open source stack, from kernel to desktop, from cloud to embedded. And we continue to expand our range of offerings to bring our security, management and developer experience to the smallest Linux environments and devices. Our team is also interested in business problems - building things reliably, efficiently and cost-effectively, and we have to learn to speak the language of our customers and their industries.
Beyond an expected Automotive expertise, this career opportunity requires a unique blend of skills. Successful candidates will know Linux well and be proficient coders and scripters. They will have experience of low-level Linux boot, BIOS, firmware and embedded software development methodologies. They also enjoy the pace of change and diversity of client engagements with driven and ambitious technology entrepreneurs. Competitive, business-focused technologists at heart, they are also dedicated team players that take pride in team and company wins.
We often say that our field engineers have 'the hardest job at Canonical' because customers can ask about any aspect of our solutions and products and expect a thoughtful, well-informed answer. We always want to do the best thing for our partners and customers, regardless of our company interests, and field engineers are the people we trust to ensure that is true.
Location : This is a home-based role, we are hiring worldwide.
What your day will look like
Engage customers during presales to gather requirements and explain our technology
Liaise with other Canonical's experts (mastering the Cloud, Kubernetes, Security or Safety, etc) to aggregate our collective knowledge into comprehensive solutions for our prospective clients
Participate to the delivery of select projects related to Embedded Linux, including demos and PoCs
Convey market requirements to key stakeholders in our organization, and sometimes participate to the development or refining of generic solutions to unlock market potential
Be both a customer advocate and a trusted advisor to Canonical
If you have a passion for the latest open source technologies applied to Automotive, if you want to play an active role in building Software Defined Vehicles, if you are curious with a will to learn how to leverage and adapt Cloud technologies to the embedded world, you will love working at Canonical.
What we are looking for in you
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or related technical field
Extensive Linux experience - Debian or Ubuntu preferred
Solid embedded Linux experience - Yocto or RTOS
Fluency in Golang, Python, C, C++, or Rust
Professional written and spoken English in addition to the local language
Excellent communication and presentation skills

description:
Acclaro combines cultural and language expertise with AI technology to help brands grow their global presence, connect with customers, and mean something to them. As a trusted partner to some of the world’s biggest brands and fastest-growing global companies, our mission is to harness the powerful combination of human expertise and cutting-edge technology. We focus on putting brands into the heads, hearts, and hands of people everywhere. Our AI-powered business management and language platform ensures a faster time to market with measurable results, while our global team of language, country, and technology experts crafts localization strategies that empower our customers to succeed in any market.
Are you an experienced localization professional or linguistic QA specialist?
We are seeking seasoned Farsi Linguistic Testers with a background in software localization and IT terminology to join our global linguistic community. In this role, you will perform linguistic QA on cutting-edge software applications and AI models for the Farsi market. If you bring strong LQA experience, deep cultural expertise, and own an M-Series Mac, we want to partner with you.
Position Overview
Language Pair : English to Farsi
Domain : Information Technology (IT), AI Models & Software Localization
Experience Level : Experienced (2+ years in Linguistic QA or Linguistic Testing)
Hardware Requirement : Must own a Mac device with an M-series chip (M1, M2, M3, M4, or newer). Note: This is an absolute technical requirement for our secure testing environment.
Employment type: Freelance / Independent contractor
Responsibilities
As a Senior Farsi Linguistic Tester , you will:
Execute Linguistic QA: Conduct rigorous linguistic, stylistic, and functional testing on localized Farsi software interfaces and AI-generated content.
Bug Tracking & Reporting: Identify, log, and regress linguistic errors, visual layout glitches (e.g. truncations, rendering/font issues, alignment), and functional defects using standard issue-tracking workflows.
Terminology & Style Guide Enforcement: Ensure absolute adherence to project glossaries, style guides, and brand-specific localization standards.
Contextual & Cultural Validation: Verify that localized content is culturally appropriate, idiomatically precise, and tailored for the Farsi market.
Collaborate with Lead Engineers: Provide constructive feedback and linguistic solutions to remote localization managers and QA leads in clear English.
To qualify for this position, candidates must meet the following criteria:
Professional Experience: Minimum 2+ years of hands-on experience in Linguistic QA, software localization testing, proofreading, or professional translation (English into Farsi).
Linguistic Proficiency: Native fluency in Farsi with exceptional command of grammar, typography, and orthography, paired with professional-level written English skills.
Hardware Specification (Mandatory): Active access to a Mac computer equipped with an Apple Silicon M-series chip (M1, M2, M3, M4, or newer).
LQA Methodology: Proven ability to differentiate between critical linguistic bugs, cosmetic layout defects, and preferential stylistic changes.
Cultural Competency: A strong, intuitive grasp of modern Farsi cultural nuances, localized language trends, and regional idiomatic expressions.
Technical Aptitude: Comfort navigating new software interfaces, adhering to detailed testing guidelines, and reporting technical/linguistic bugs clearly in English.
Work Environment: A reliable high-speed internet connection and a dedicated workspace suitable for remote, independent contract work.
Attention to Quality: Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to consistently identify minor grammatical, formatting, and user-interface (UI) errors.
Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere, managing your own hours around project deadlines.
